raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-ALB-CitizenServiceDelivery",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "ADISA and MIPA lack experience in executing large donor-funded operations, creating risks of implementation delays and non-compliance with World Bank fiduciary requirements.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish a dedicated Project Management Unit (PMU) within ADISA staffed with qualified financial, procurement, and administrative specialists, supported initially by the Ministry of Finance CFCU.",
      "evidence": "Neither MIPA, nor the recently constituted ADISA have previous experience in implementation of large donor funded operations"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "ADISA is a newly created agency without an established procurement track record, leading to a high procurement risk rating and potential contracting delays.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Utilize the established CFCU under the Ministry of Finance during the PPF stage, hire experienced procurement specialists for the PMU, and prepare a detailed Project Operational Manual.",
      "evidence": "Since ADISA is a newly-created agency and the PMU is not yet fully set up, the procurement risk rating is high."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Substantial financial management risk due to unproven accounting and internal control systems across newly participating budgetary and non-budgetary entities.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit two finance specialists for the PMU, procure dedicated accounting software, document financial management procedures in a Financial Management Manual, and utilize CFCU oversight initially.",
      "evidence": "The overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Line ministries, agency heads, and field staff may resist ceding front-office customer service functions to ADISA or adapting legacy administrative workflows.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement a structured change management and stakeholder outreach program, and leverage strong strategic coordination through the Inter-Ministerial Public Services Committee.",
      "evidence": "Ministries, agencies and individual civil servants may not welcome ceding the front office function to CSC. Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts to improve back-office functions."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Construction of the central Citizen Service Center (CSC) facility in Tirana generates localized environmental impacts including dust, noise, waste, and site safety risks.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Integrate the World Bank OP 4.01 compliant Environmental Management Plan (EMP) into construction bidding documents, assign PMU oversight, and enforce contractor compliance.",
      "evidence": "Potential environmental impacts that are associated with new construction include dust and noise, waste generation, material supply, use of machinery on site"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Focusing resources on high-end urban Citizen Service Centers and web-based e-services risks excluding poor, rural, elderly, and vulnerable populations who lack digital access.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Maintain existing physical service access points, establish assisted digital access outreach centers in post offices/internet cafes, establish call centers, and track access indicators disaggregated by income and gender.",
      "evidence": "focus on state-of-the-art means for service delivery, such as online services or high-end urban CSCs, will diminish access of the poor and vulnerable"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "An overly compressed reform schedule across multiple phases creates risks of slippage in business process re-engineering, IT automation, and facility construction.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Sequence implementation to deliver early wins via citizen feedback and performance monitoring while structuring loan disbursements around 5 key Results-Based Financing DLIs through 2020.",
      "evidence": "The Government’s timeline for the reform is very ambitious."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Achieving reform objectives across more than 10 government agencies involves complex inter-sectoral coordination that could lead to administrative bottlenecks.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Empower the Prime Minister's Delivery Unit (DU) and the Inter-Ministerial Public Services Committee to actively track implementation progress, unblock institutional barriers, and enforce inter-agency cooperation.",
      "evidence": "Inter-sectoral reforms, especially those that involve more than a dozen government agencies, necessarily entail complex coordination."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Incomplete database archives, missing national ID numbers in key registries (e.g., property, transport), and legal disputes over ownership impair database interoperability and service automation.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide targeted technical assistance to digitize legacy records, populate unique ID numbers, optimize databases, and mandate connection to the NAIS Government Gateway interoperability platform.",
      "evidence": "The National ID number is missing for most records, only 45 to 50 percent of the archive is digitized, and legal issues over ownership remain"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Process re-engineering requires enacting broad legislative amendments through omnibus legislation; parliamentary delays or legislative resistance could block necessary legal reforms.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Form specialized ministerial working groups to prepare legal inventories and re-engineering plans early, under the oversight of the Technical Inter-ministerial Committee.",
      "evidence": "Reform of government services and repeal of licenses, permits, and approvals will be implemented through omnibus legislation, expected to be passed by the end of 2016."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Modest national internet penetration (60%) limits direct citizen adoption of online transactional services (Level 3/4 automation).",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish physical CSC one-stop-shops and train post office, local government, and internet cafe staff to provide assisted internet access for online service delivery.",
      "evidence": "modest levels of internet penetration at only 60 internet users per 100 people in 2013"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Implementing agencies lack sufficient technical personnel with expertise in software architecture, database management, and process re-engineering.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Deploy US$5 million in Technical Assistance funding to hire specialized international and local technical experts to support NAIS, ADISA, and line agencies.",
      "evidence": "the authorities do not have staff with the technical skills and experience needed to implement the reform process."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "High upfront capital investments and ongoing software licensing, operation, and maintenance costs for CSC and IT platforms could strain government fiscal resources.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Explore public-private partnership (PPP) financing options for CSC construction/operation and capture budget savings from front-office efficiency gains and process re-engineering.",
      "evidence": "There are significant upfront financial costs associated with the development of the CSC, business process reengineering, digitization, automation, training staff and educating citizens"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Discrepancies between official internal agency processing metrics and actual citizen experience obscure real service delivery delays and impede accurate performance management.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Deploy proactive text-message (SMS) and phone-based Citizen Feedback Mechanisms (CFM) alongside periodic independent third-party user surveys to validate administrative tracking data.",
      "evidence": "The data submitted by the IPRO office on the other hand routinely records that almost all applications are processed within the required six days."
    }
  ]
}
